title: Post-Quantum Perfect Zero-Knowledge Arguments for NP From Any One-Way Permutation
authors: Frédéric Dupuis, Rémi Ligez, Khaireddine Medhioub, Louis Salvail, Louis-Charles Thibodeau
abstract: In this paper, we show for the first time that post-quantum one-way permutations are sufficient for perfect zero-knowledge classical arguments for all of NP with security guaranteed against quantum adversaries. We first establish that Naor, Ostrovsky,Venkatesen, and Yung's bit commitment scheme built from any permutation using interactive hashing, called the NOVY scheme, is sum-binding and collapse-binding against quantum polynomial-time committers provided the permutation is post-quantum one-way. We then show that the collapse-binding property of the NOVY scheme allows for Blum's perfect zero-knowledge argument for HAMCYCLE to remain so exactly as it stands against quantum adversaries.
summary: This paper achieves a significant theoretical result by showing that post-quantum one-way permutations are sufficient to build perfect zero-knowledge argument systems for all of NP, even against quantum adversaries. The authors achieve this by analyzing the 'novy' commitment scheme and employing advanced techniques involving quantum super-operators to prove the necessary security properties.
main_problem: To demonstrate that post-quantum one-way permutations are sufficient to construct perfect zero-knowledge classical argument systems for all of NP, secure against quantum adversaries.
main_result: The authors show that using the 'novy' bit commitment scheme, they establish a post-quantum perfect zero-knowledge argument system for all of NP with a soundness error bounded by 14/15.
method: The proof involves constructing and analyzing quantum super-operators ($\Omega, \Xi, \Psi$) that model the entire interactive proof protocol, comparing it to the simulator's action to prove zero-knowledge.
model_or_system: The underlying model relies on the existence of post-quantum one-way permutations and the use of the 'novy' interactive hashing commitment scheme to build the argument system for NP.
key_observables: The final state of the verifier after the protocol ($\Xi_{G',t,ch,H',u}(ho)$) and the output state of the simulator ($ho_8$).
important_parameters: The soundness error (14/15), the security assumption (post-quantum one-way permutations), and the structure of the commitment scheme (novy).
main_assumptions: The existence of post-quantum one-way permutations and the perfect hiding property of the bit commitment scheme ($\Pi$).

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the properties of the novy scheme (Theorem 1), then developing the quantum inverter ($	ext{qInvS}_{\pi}$) to prove soundness (Chunk 2), and finally formalizing the zero-knowledge proof using super-operators ($\Omega, \Xi, \Psi$) to prove the final zero-knowledge result (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of quantum-resistant cryptography by connecting fundamental computational complexity classes (NP) to quantum-secure primitives (one-way permutations).
